newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain to play key role in Stet expansion.
newsitem.headline: Spain to play key role in Stet expansion.

text.p: Italian state telecommunications holding company Stet said on Monday Spain would play a key role in its European expansion.
"Spain has a very important role in Stet's international strategy," said Marina del Pozo, who led Stet negotiations in Spain in the bidding for Retevision.

Earlier on Monday it was announced Stet and the Spanish utility Endesa will lead a consortium with a 30.9 percent stake each for the 60 percent privatisation of Retevision, which will be Spain's second telephone operator.
The consortium, including some saving banks, the electrical firm Union Fenosa, and the regional Euskaltel, now has four weeks to present its final offer.
It is directly competing with another consortium called Opera, comprised of Spanish bank BCH, France Telecom and Sprint, and possibly with a third competitor.

Luis Rodrigo, who represents Endesa in the consortium, said if they gain control of Retevision, they will be counting on minimum assets of 400 billion pesetas plus other funds to make "a very substantial" investment in developing its own telecommunications network in Spain.
Rodrigo added that if the group won the auction, it would also have the backing of 12,000 kilometres of fibre optic network.
"There's a willingness to reach a deal with Iberdrola, Fenosa, Enher and Hidrocantabrico, so all the electrical firms can make up part of our infrastructure," Rodrigo said.
Rodrigo added they also intended to reach agreement with the second mobile phone operator Airtel.
Endesa and Union Fenosa have a stake which totals around 16 percent in Airtel, and Rodrigo said in future they would like Stet to have the same role British Telecom has now in the mobile operator.
After BT announced a key alliance with Airtel's competitor Telefonica de Espana, it committed itself to sell its current 16 percent holding in Airtel.
